applies_why: The judge text issues an UNDERDETERMINED verdict whose stated ground is that the single verse Matthew 1:16 admits both readings, which is exactly the move this rule governs.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that admits both readings is such a verse.
room: The phrase 'A verse that admits both readings is such a verse': either it merely classifies such verses, or it folds them into the ban on ever grounding STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED in one verse's non-statement; I weighed the second reading as the plain sense.
why: The judge made Matthew 1:16's admitting both readings the stated ground of an UNDERDETERMINED verdict, which K-S2 says is never a ground for that verdict.
